properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-11, in his words: "reflow2 has a capability to return to the agent any systems engineering data (not view) and the agent can render it. would like to actually demonstrate this in the docs of these examples of different views of reflow2 using this rendering type construct." Nothing here is intent.

⭐⭐ THIS IS ALREADY THE RECORDED DIRECTION, AND IT IS UNBUILT. `docs/viewpoints.md` §"Direction (the rest of BL-40)" says it almost exactly: "once the catalogue's shape has settled here, move the projection data into core as typed read tools on the MCP surface (the `flow_report` shape — facts plus confessions — is the template), so the in-session agent renders views deterministically instead of re-deriving them through an LLM, which is exactly where extrapolation would creep back in." Same shape as `req:what-next` last month — accepted intent, blocker unexamined, nobody built it. This is not a new idea to decide; it is an old idea to finish.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, measured 2026-08-11:
  typed report-shaped read tools on the MCP surface   15  (graph_report, flow_report, maturity_report,
                                                          granularity_report, ility_report, readiness_report,
                                                          evidence_report, coverage_report, seam_report,
                                                          budget_report, release_report, confirmation_ledger,
                                                          changelog_view, claim_report, graph_report_markdown)
  tools/render_views.py                               44 KB, renders 10 DoDAF-informed viewpoints
  docs/design/views.html                              323 KB of rendered output
So the DATA side is largely built and the RENDER side exists as deterministic Python that writes one HTML file nobody links from the reading order.

⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR DOING IT IS FROM TODAY, AND IT IS DAMNING. Every one of these is a hand-maintained claim ABOUT THE GRAPH that the graph could have answered:
  · `docs/overview.md:52` says the schema has 60 edge types. The export stamp says 61.
  · `docs/three-axes.md` says axis Z is "MISSING". The graph holds 111 DesignEpochs, 133 TemporalFacts,
    114 Snapshots and 362 ChangeEvents. The doc that would tell a reader whether time is modelled says it is not.
  · 3 of 4 deferrals spot-checked in `requirements-coverage.md` were wrong (SP-3b, GS-17, 3AX-5).
  · `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` lists dead_end, disconnected_community and single_point_of_failure
    as deferred. All three are built.
A rendered doc cannot make any of these mistakes, because it has no opinion of its own.

⚠️⚠️ THE CENTRAL RISK, and it is this project's own doctrine pointed at the proposal. `viewpoints.md` rule 1: "A projection may sort, group, count and draw — it may not infer, default, or improvise." An LLM's default behaviour IS to improvise, and Anthony's own standing position (UAF/DoDAF-trained: views must be pure projections; a renderer fill-in is a reflow2 defect) makes an improvised sentence in a rendered doc a DEFECT REPORT, not a cosmetic issue. The existing Python renderer cannot improvise by construction. Moving rendering to the agent trades staleness for extrapolation — and the doc's own Direction paragraph names that trade explicitly as the reason to move the DATA into typed tools first, so the agent has less room to invent.

⚠️ SECOND RISK: DETERMINISM AND THE DIFF. A committed file rendered by an LLM churns on every regeneration — different wording, same facts — so `git diff` stops meaning "the design changed". `render_views.py` is deterministic and byte-stable; an agent is not.

⚠️ THIRD, AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT CALL NOT A BUG: confessions become PUBLIC. Every renderer here is also a probe, and what it cannot project it confesses. Rendering the outward-facing docs means reflow2's adoption surface carries reflow2's own gaps to a first-time reader. `partnership.md` argues credibility is decided at the front door. A confessing doc reads either as unusually honest or as unfinished, and which one it is depends on the reader, not on us.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) LIVE ONLY — the agent renders a view on demand from the typed tools; nothing is committed. Never stale by construction. Costs the browsable artifact: a stranger on GitHub sees no docs, and docs ARE the adoption surface.
(b) COMMITTED + CHECKED — render into committed files and add a CI step that re-renders and diffs, so a stale doc fails the build. Turns doc staleness into a gate, which is the actual disease. Needs determinism, which argues for keeping the renderer deterministic (Python/Rust) rather than an LLM.
(c) HYBRID — prose docs that EMBED rendered sections between markers, regenerated and diff-checked. Smallest change; keeps the argument-shaped docs intact and puts the facts under the gate. Every number that went stale today lives in an embeddable section.
(d) DEMONSTRATION ONLY — pick two or three docs, render them as worked examples of the capability, leave the rest prose. This is closest to what Anthony literally asked for, and it is the cheapest way to find out whether the output is any good before committing the whole doc set to it.

📌 SEQUENCING FINDING, recorded because it changes what to do NEXT. Anthony asked in the same breath for `genesis.md`, `artifact-linking.md`, `impact-propagation.md`, `gap-surfacing.md` and `heal-process.md` to be rewritten as outward-facing prose. Those five describe what `genesis`, `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts`, `propagate_from`, `detect_gaps` and `propose_heal` DO AND RETURN — which makes them the FIRST candidates to become projections, not prose. Hand-rewriting 661 lines into a format that may be replaced is the wasteful order. Deciding (d) first costs one doc's worth of work and tells you whether the other four should be written at all.

═══ RESTATED BY ANTHONY, 2026-09-16, FIVE WEEKS LATER AND STILL UNBUILT — with a new leg ═══
In his words: *"the documents should be a realization of what reflow2 is and be updated as reflow2 is developed and improved. The contents of the documents should be linked in the reflow2 design graph, so when the graph changes, they are changed. This is almost like what we do for the changelog.md document that is generated by how the graph changes. The only difference is that these should be authored to be easily readable."*

He raised it because the answer to a question he had just asked (must artifacts follow a recognized standard, must a number be checkable, must a design close) *"used to be stated right in the docs that we created from the beginning"*. It was — docs/partnership.md opens with "how do you know it didn't hallucinate?" and maps every LLM failure mode to its check — and the graph did not know that document exists.

⭐ THE NEW LEG IS THE LINK, NOT THE RENDER. The 2026-08-11 framing asked who renders. Today's asks that a document be LINKED to the nodes it explains so that a change to those nodes reaches the document — the same ripple `propagate_change` gives code. That is a different mechanism from rendering and it is cheaper: the deterministic half (WHICH document is owed a rewrite, because of WHICH change) is graph work; the written half (the readable rewrite) is the agent's, reviewed by the person. The most reflow2 can honestly promise is that no document goes stale UNNOTICED — the promise it already makes about code.

THE MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-16, from the export:
  · 55 markdown files under docs/ (feedback/, design/, trials/ excluded). 31 registered as Artifacts; 24 NOT — and the 24 are the FOUNDING set: vision.md, overview.md, partnership.md, three-axes.md, viewpoints.md, genesis.md, gap-surfacing.md, heal-process.md, graph-analysis.md, interaction-surfaces.md, roadmap-and-planned-epochs.md, requirements-coverage.md. The docs that say why reflow2 exists are the ones the design cannot see.
  · 54 DOCUMENTS edges from 36 artifacts, every one with a checksum — so `reconcile_artifacts` notices when a DOC changes on disk. Nothing notices when the GRAPH changes under a doc: `crates/reflow2-core/src/artifact.rs` says PROPAGATE "deliberately does not traverse DOCUMENTS yet — whether a change should ripple to every doc that mentions it is BL-26's open decision, not an oversight." That open decision, from July, is exactly the leg he asked for today.
  · Already passing the deletion test and generated: CHANGELOG.md (`cap:changelog-view`), docs/skills-and-tools.md (a CI gate). docs/viewpoints.md is rendered by `render_views.py` and not registered.

(e) ⭐ ADDED 2026-09-16, composes with (c): LINK, RIPPLE, REWRITE. (1) Register the founding docs and draw DOCUMENTS from each to the INTENT it explains — requirements and decisions, never to every mechanism it mentions, or a doc explaining `loop_status` is stale weekly. (2) PROPAGATE traverses DOCUMENTS and reports each document explaining a changed node as owed a rewrite, beside the artifacts it already reports — closing BL-26 with "yes, as a stale-report, never an auto-edit". (3) The rewrite is prose, so it is the agent's, and the checksum is reset when the person accepts it. Generation (b) stays right for a document that IS a list; (e) is for the ones that argue. ⚠️ Cost: the edges are a day of reading, and drawing them to the wrong grain makes every doc permanently stale.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2's outward-facing docs be RENDERED from the graph by the agent, rather than hand-written prose that goes stale?
properties.rationale:
Four hand-maintained claims about the graph were found wrong in a single day, and every one was answerable from the graph. The data side is 15 typed tools already built and the direction is already recorded in viewpoints.md as the rest of BL-40. What is genuinely open is who renders — an LLM buys freshness and risks the extrapolation this project treats as a defect; deterministic code keeps the doctrine and keeps the diff meaningful.

SHARPENED 2026-09-16 rather than duplicated: Anthony restated the same want five weeks on, which is itself the finding (an idea recorded and not built gets re-asked). The restatement adds one leg the August framing lacked — the LINK from a document to what it explains, so a graph change reaches the document — and that leg is cheaper than any rendering option and independent of who renders.
